title: Equidimensional closed fibre of a finite type domain over a valuation ring
statement: Let $A$ be a valuation ring, meaning an integral domain such that for each nonzero $a\in K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ either $a\in A$ or $a^{-1}\in A$, and put $k=A/\mathfrak m_A$ for its residue field. Let $D$ be an integral domain containing $A$ as a subring and finite type as an $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Form the algebras $D_k=D\otimes_Ak$ and $D_K=D\otimes_AK$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with multiplication $(d\otimes a)(e\otimes b)=de\otimes ab$. If $D_k\ne0$, then $\dim D_k=\dim D_K$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], and $\operatorname{Spec}D_k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is equidimensional: every irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] has topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] equal to $\dim D_K$.

source.place: Tag 00QK (lemma-finite-type-domain-over-valuation-ring-dim-fibres), statement including its final equidimensionality assertion

proof.text: Put $F=D_K$, $E=D_k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-generic-fibre-localization-domain-irreducible], $F$ is the localization of $D$ at the nonzero elements of $A$, and is a nonzero domain. If $d_1,\ldots,d_r$ generate $D$ over $A$, their tensor images generate $F$ over $K$ and $E$ over $k$: expand each pure tensor using its polynomial expression in the $d_i$ and use tensor balancing. The dimension/transcendence-degree theorem [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-domain-dimension-trdeg] gives a finite integer $d=\dim F=\operatorname{trdeg}_K L$, where $L=\operatorname{Frac}(F)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-components], applied to the finite type domain $F$, its local topological dimension at every prime is $d$, since its spectrum has the single component $\operatorname{Spec}F$; the spectrum/ring comparison identifies the two dimensions.

source.place: Tag 00QK, first paragraph of proof; dimension finiteness and the generic local dimension expanded with Tag 00P0 and Tag 00OT

proof.text: Fix a prime $Q$ of $E$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection] its contraction $\mathfrak q\subset D$ lies over $\mathfrak m_A$, with $Q$ the corresponding fibre prime. By [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-components], $n=\dim_Q\operatorname{Spec}E$ is a finite nonnegative integer. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-dimension-bounded-open-upstairs] at $\mathfrak q$ to get an open neighbourhood $V$ where every local fibre dimension is at most $n$. A nonempty open in the spectrum of the domain $D$ contains $(0)$: its closed complement cannot contain $(0)$ without containing its closure $V_D(0)=\operatorname{Spec}D$. At $(0)$ the base prime is $(0)$ and the fibre prime in $F$ is $(0)$, since the localization $D\hookrightarrow F$ is injective. Step 1 evaluates this local dimension as $d$. Thus $d\le n$.

source.place: Tag 00QK, proof, first inequality using Tag 00QH

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-over-polynomial-algebra] to $A	o D$, $\mathfrak q$ and $n$. It gives $g
otin\mathfrak q$ and a finite type, everywhere quasi-finite $A$-algebra map $\alpha:A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]	o B=D_g$. Since $g
e0$, $B$ is a domain containing $A$. Write $H=B\otimes_AK$ and $T=B\otimes_Ak$. For $c=K,k$, identify $(D\otimes_Ac)\otimes_DB$ with $B\otimes_Ac$ by $(d\otimes c_0)\otimes b\mapsto db\otimes c_0$, inverse $b\otimes c_0\mapsto(1\otimes c_0)\otimes b$; tensor balancing verifies these inverse maps. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change] to $D	o D_g$ shows that $H$ and $T$ are the away localizations of $F$ and $E$ at the respective images of $g$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open], $\operatorname{Spec}T$ is the open $D_E( ar g)$ containing $Q$. The open-subspace local-dimension theorem therefore gives $\dim_{Q_g}\operatorname{Spec}T=n$ at the corresponding point $Q_g$. In particular $T
e0$.

source.place: Tag 00QK, proof, quasi-finite polynomial chart from Tag 00QE; the fibre localization and local-dimension invariance are made explicit

proof.text: For $c=K$ and $c=k$, tensor $\alpha$ with $c$ and use [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-scalar-extension] to obtain $\alpha_c:c[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\to B\otimes_Ac$. This map is finite type and quasi-finite at every prime by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-four-rings]: the square has top rings $A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$, $B$, and bottom rings $c[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$, $B\otimes_Ac$; each element of the last ring is a sum $\sum_i b_i\otimes c_i=\sum_i(b_i\otimes1)\alpha_c(c_i)$. This is precisely the finite-sum hypothesis of that node. Both fibre algebras are finite type over their fields, generated by the images of $d_1,\ldots,d_r,g^{-1}$.

source.place: Tag 00QK, proof, the induced polynomial maps on the two fibres; scalar extension and quasi-finiteness justified by Tag 00PN

proof.text: Suppose for a contradiction that $d<n$. The localization $H=F_g$ embeds in $L$ and has fraction field $L$: every fraction of elements of $F$ is already a fraction of elements of $H$, and conversely $H\subset L$. If $\alpha_K$ were injective, its variable images in $L$ would be algebraically independent, since evaluating any nonzero polynomial would remain nonzero. They would then be $n$ distinct elements and would give $\operatorname{trdeg}_KL\ge n$ by [def-kun-transcendence-degree], contradicting step 1. Hence choose a nonzero $f=\sum_Ia_It^I\in\ker\alpha_K$.

source.place: Tag 00QK, proof, existence of a nonzero generic-fibre polynomial kernel when the dimension is less than n

proof.text: Among the finitely many nonzero coefficients $a_I$ choose $b=a_J$ such that $a_I/b\in A$ for every $I$. Here is the finite induction that gives this choice without a rank or discreteness assumption: start with one coefficient $b$; for the next nonzero coefficient $a$, either $a/b\in A$ and keep $b$, or $b/a\in A$ and replace $b$ by $a$. Previously admitted coefficients $c$ then satisfy $c/a=(c/b)(b/a)\in A$. Thus $h=b^{-1}f$ has all coefficients in $A$ and its $J$-coefficient is $1$. Its image in $H$ is zero. Since $B$ is a domain containing $A$, [lem-weil-pbc-generic-fibre-localization-domain-irreducible] applied to $A\to B$ shows that $B\to H$ is the localization of $B$ at the nonzero elements of $A$; this map is injective: an element killed in the localization is killed by some nonzero $s\in A$, hence was zero. Therefore $\alpha(h)=0$ in $B$.

source.place: Tag 00QK, proof, coefficient of minimal valuation; finite divisibility induction and torsion cancellation written out

proof.text: Reduce the coefficients of $h$ modulo $\mathfrak m_A$. The resulting $\bar h\in k[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ is nonzero because its $J$-coefficient is $1$. Tensoring the equality $\alpha(h)=0$ with $k$ gives $\alpha_k(\bar h)=0$. Apply [lem-trf-quasi-finite-polynomial-kernel-dimension-drop] to this map, whose finite type and quasi-finiteness were checked in step 4: $\dim\operatorname{Spec}T<n$. But $Q_g$ belongs to this spectrum, and its local dimension $n$ is at most the global dimension, since the entire spectrum is an open neighbourhood of $Q_g$ in the defining minimum [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]. This contradicts step 3. We conclude $n\le d$, and together with step 2, $n=d$.

source.place: Tag 00QK, proof, nonzero residue-fibre relation and strict dimension-drop contradiction

proof.text: The prime $Q$ was arbitrary, so every point of $\operatorname{Spec}E$ has local dimension $d$. The dimension-as-supremum-of-local-dimensions theorem [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions] gives global dimension $d$; this is a nonempty supremum because $E\ne0$: [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] states that absence of prime ideals is equivalent to being the zero ring. The spectrum/ring comparison then gives $\dim E=d=\dim F$. For equidimensionality, [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes] writes each component as $V(\mathfrak p)$ for a minimal prime $\mathfrak p$ of $E$. At the point $\mathfrak p$, this is the unique component containing it: a component $V(\mathfrak r)$ through it has $\mathfrak r\subseteq\mathfrak p$, hence $\mathfrak r=\mathfrak p$ by minimality. The dimension-at-point/components theorem now identifies the dimension of that component with $\dim_{\mathfrak p}\operatorname{Spec}E=d$. This proves every clause.

source.place: Tag 00QK, final assertion and initial reduction to constant local fibre dimension; Tag 00OT component formula
